text: The Krebs cycle is the step people lose marks on, because it is the middle of a chain and easy to isolate.
Your notes also call it the citric acid cycle. Same thing, two names.
Worth knowing, though your notes do not say it: it runs inside the mitochondria.
It runs twice for every glucose.
Why twice, do you think, rather than once?
Because one glucose is split in two earlier on, so each half goes round. Your notes give the number; the reason is the useful part.
It makes N A D H and F A D H 2, and those feed the electron transport chain.
So what does the Krebs cycle hand on, and to what?
N A D H and F A D H 2, handed to the electron transport chain.
Two names, twice per glucose, and it feeds the next stage. That is the whole of it.
